message_source_quote: The approach builds on the white-bear steering (WBS) paper's insight that a *stance* direction (not content) can amplify concept readability through the J-lens.
writeup_source_quote: The white-bear steering (WBS) paper shows that a stance direction built from the think/don't-think contrast in WorkspaceBench's directed_modulation items lifts the plain J-lens readout on association from 0.14 to 0.83 pass@10.
rationale: Both documents identify WBS (white-bear steering) by name as the prior work whose think/don't-think stance-direction method this task's method builds on and deliberately diverges from via a new think/conceal contrast. Both state the same novelty claim almost verbatim (WBS tested think/don't-think which works and hold/mention which doesn't; this adds a third, think/conceal, with comparable dose profile and a distinct-but-related direction at cosine 0.85), so there is no material difference in source treatment or novelty framing between the message and the write-up.
